subject: Reserved GPU mix — performance-per-dollar, memory constraints and SLA packaging
messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@clearwave.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearwave.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sizing & pricing for reserved capacity — workload details attached

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have a production use case (real-time document enrichment + nightly batch embeddings) and are evaluating reserved capacity with Redwood. Attached is a short workload profile: ~320 qps sustained (peak 900 qps for short bursts) for token-limited text-gen (avg 120 tokens response), and batch jobs that run overnight at ~2M tokens/hour.

Primary concerns:
- Perf/$: maximize throughput per dollar for high-volume inference.
- Latency tail: want P95 < 120ms for the real-time path.
- Memory: some models require 80+GB workspaces for large instruction-tuned LMs.
- SLAs + credits for sustained misses.

Specifically ask: how do A100 (40/80GB), H100 (80/94GB), and L40S (48GB) compare for this mix when packaged as a Reserved commit? Also what discount tiers do you offer for 12/24 month commits, and do you support hybrid pools (mix of GPU types) with deterministic routing to meet latency SLOs?

Please include any recommended canary plan for rollouts and an initial cost estimate. I attached the workload CSV.

Best,
Maria
VP Product, Clearwave Analytics

Attachments: workload_profile_q1.csv (attachment stub)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@clearwave.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing & pricing for reserved capacity — initial sizing + options

Maria — thanks for the workload details and the CSV. High level takeaways: your real-time path needs low P95 and steady qps; batch is cost-dominant. We believe a hybrid reserved pool will hit your goals while optimizing spend.

Quick summary of viable packaging options (prices are indicative; see attached quote):

1) Latency-first hybrid (recommended for product-launch):
   - H100 (80/94GB) x 6 for the real-time group (handles low-latency, large-memory models)
   - L40S x 8 for batch and lower-priority inference (cheaper perf/$ for throughput)
   - Dedicated routing: latency policy routes requests to H100; overflow/batch to L40S.
   - Throughput guarantee: 320 sustained qps across pool, 900 qps burst capacity using autoscale/burst credits.
   - 12-month reserved commit: mid-tier discount; 18% off list for this mix (see quote).

2) Cost-maximized throughput:
   - A100 80GB x 10 (good perf/$ on high-token workloads when quantized)
   - Best for batch-heavy workloads, P95 slightly higher for the real-time tail unless model sharding is used.
   - 24-month commit: up to 24% discount band.

3) Single-GPU simplicity (if procurement prefers one SKU):
   - H100-only, smaller capacity. Easier for compliance/auditing but higher unit cost.

Tradeoffs & technical notes:
- Memory: H100 80/94GB is best when you need >48GB working set; A100 80GB can work with model sharding but adds latency variability. L40S memory (48GB) is often fine for quantized or trimmed models.
- Perf/$: L40S beats H100 for batch throughput on many decoder-only use cases; H100 is stronger on latency-sensitive large-context models. A100 sits in the middle when using 80GB variants.
- Quantization: 4-bit/8-bit quant can drastically improve perf/$ on A100/L40S but must be validated for your model fidelity.
- Canary plan: 2-week canary on 10% traffic (H100 path), compare P95/P99 and token-level quality metrics, then ramp to 50% before full cutover.

I attached a draft quote (redwood_quote_v1.pdf) and a quick perf matrix. Marcus — adding you for throughput guarantees and SLA language.

Next steps: can we do a short call Wednesday to align on preferred mix and finalize a sample pricing band?

Thanks,
Sooj
Soojinn Lee
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_quote_v1.pdf (attachment stub); performance_matrix_q12027.xlsx (attachment stub)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@clearwave.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing & pricing for reserved capacity — throughput guarantees and SLA notes

Maria / Sooj — quick technical + commercial follow-up from infra side.

We can commit to a throughput SLO for the reserved pool shape. Proposed commercial guarantee:
- Sustained throughput SLO: 320 qps (measured as 5-min rolling average) with 95% uptime per month.
- Burst capacity: baseline pool + configurable burst credits to 900 qps for up to 2 hours/day.
- Credits: SLA credit tiered if monthly measured availability for the SLO < 95% (see quote appendix).

Operational suggestion (hybrid mix):
- Start with 6x H100 + 8x L40S (Sooj's latency-first config).
- Route all latency-critical requests to a pinned H100 subset (dedicated instances), leave rest for pooled work. Deterministic routing avoids noisy neighbor effects.
- For batch, use autoscale with spot-backed nodes where acceptable, and fall back to L40S reserved capacity for guaranteed throughput.

Memory & model-fitting guidance:
- For models requiring 80+GB workspace, use H100 94GB variants or split model across two A100/80s with careful KV cache placement.
- If you can quantize to 4-bit with minor quality delta, A100 + L40S mix becomes more attractive cost-wise.

I'll update the performance_matrix with measured tokens/sec and per-token cost for your workload and upload an updated quote by EOD.

Marcus
Director, Inference Infrastructure, Redwood Inference

Attachment: infra_perf_notes.txt (attachment stub)

From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@clearwave.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearwave.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 09:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing & pricing for reserved capacity — follow-up questions

Thanks — helpful detail. A few clarifying questions before the call:

1) If we choose hybrid (H100 + L40S), can we guarantee routing determinism during spikes so our latency-critical path never gets starved? Who owns the rollback?
2) For the SLA credit bands, can we see sample language (we need consumer-friendly credit calculation for procurement).
3) For models with 80+GB working set, is there any loss in latency when sharding across two A100s compared to running on single H100 94GB?
4) Pricing: you mentioned 18% (12m) and up to 24% (24m). Can you provide a banded table (3 tiers) with clear list price, committed discount, and effective perf/$ per token for our workload?

Also: we need a canary proposal that includes rollback triggers (quality regression >1.5% BLEU-equivalent metric or P95 > 200ms).

If you can send the revised quote + SLA appendix before our call Friday, we can get procurement moving.

Cheers,
Maria

Attachments: none

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@clearwave.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 08:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing & pricing for reserved capacity — quote appendix & canary plan

Maria — attaching the requested materials and answering the bullets inline:  

1) Routing determinism + rollback ownership:
   - We support deterministic routing rules (per-route affinity, token-budget thresholds). During spikes we reserve a small H100 buffer (10-15% of H100 pool) specifically for latency-critical keys to avoid starvation. Redwood owns routing and fallback logic; customer owns the decision to trigger rollback. We recommend an automated rollback policy: if P95 > 200ms for 3 consecutive 5-minute windows or quality metric delta exceeds threshold, traffic automatically shifts to a stable fallback model (same API surface) and we open a high-priority incident.

2) SLA credits table: attached in quote appendix (high-level: 5% credit for monthly SLO 95-97%, 15% for 90-94%, 30% for <90%). We can adjust language for your procurement team.

3) Sharding latency delta:
   - Sharding across two A100s adds serialization overhead and KV cache sync; expect an extra 20-60ms on p95 compared to single H100 94GB for large-context generative runs. If 120ms P95 is a hard cap, prefer H100 for those models.

4) Pricing bands (illustrative):
   - Tier A (12m, entry): 12% off list, effective perf/$ baseline X
   - Tier B (12m, mid): 18% off list — Sooj proposed band, good for hybrid mix
   - Tier C (24m, committed): 24% off list, includes 2x free emergency burst days per quarter
   - Attached: redwood_quote_v2.pdf with exact line items and perf/$ by token for your CSV workload.

Canary triggers (recommended):
- Rollback if quality regression >1.5% on holdout set for two consecutive runs; or
- P95 exceed 200ms for 3 continuous 5-min windows; or
- Error rate >0.5% of requests for 5 minutes.

I attached redwood_quote_v2.pdf and an updated performance_matrix_q12027.xlsx that maps your workload to per-token cost for the three GPU mixes. Please review and we can finalize terms on Friday's call.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_quote_v2.pdf (attachment stub); performance_matrix_q12027.xlsx (attachment stub)

From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@clearwave.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing & pricing for reserved capacity — next steps

Appreciate the thoroughness — the updated quote and the SLA appendix look good. Procurement wants the 12-month mid-tier (Tier B) pricing but needs an explicit clause for a one-time model migration credit if we switch model architectures within the first 6 months. Can you add that to the commercial terms?

Let's keep Friday's 11:00 AM PT slot. Please include legal and billing on that invite. I'll circulate an internal list of holdout-set metrics we want monitored during canary ahead of the call.

Thanks,
Maria
